exposure: Prior myomectomy vs. no prior myomectomy
cohort: 290 women who delivered between 2008 and 2017 with a viable intrauterine pregnancy at initial ultrasound scan and either prior myomectomy or at least one fibroid ≥ 5 cm on a prenatal scan performed at < 21 weeks' gestation
finding: Women with prior myomectomy had significantly more preterm births, due in part to more preterm, prelabor cesareans in the late preterm period.
mod_finding: Women with prior myomectomy had significantly more cesarean deliveries compared to women with fibroids who did not have prior myomectomy.
gest_age: Viable pregnancies at initial ultrasound scan
